proposition: all vectors forming the embeddings, MLP, attention matrices and hidden states are unit norm normalized.
notes: Intentionally scoped to the paper's explicit abstract statement; this record does not claim a causal explanation for nGPT performance.

proposition: The paper characterizes bisimulation-preserving linear quotient maps for finite-dimensional linear control systems under its specified observation and timing semantics.
notes: No arbitrary nonlinear quotient or unrestricted observation-map converse. Corrects the provisional domain-scaling-lab DOI 10.1016/S0005-1098(03)00255-3; that identifier was never accepted here.

proposition: The Isabelle development proves both directions of Myhill–Nerode using regular expressions; its combined theorem fixes a finite alphabet.
notes: Manuel Eberl is credited as a contributor. Source inspection is not an independent Isabelle build, nor proof of a general observation-quotient adapter.

proposition: For a finite parameter tuple, the paper establishes finite-outcome decision-comparison/garbling equivalence and extends comparisons beyond finite outcomes through its standard-measure formulation.
notes: Preserve the Borel-field setup, closed bounded convex loss-vector sets, and state-independent kernel. Theorem 8 concerns auxiliary bounded standard-measure supports. No unrestricted general-state converse is imported.

proposition: For a bounded matrix family, arbitrary-switching asymptotic stability is characterized by joint spectral radius below one.
notes: Definitions 1.1–1.2 concern asymptotic product growth. This does not make per-step singular extrema sharp iff tests; stabilizability concerns a vanishing product operator norm, not merely one initial vector.

proposition: The lower-spectral-radius algorithm has a convergence theorem for restricted finite real asymptotically rank-one families with the specified invariant-cone and antinorm hypotheses.
notes: Every nonempty product must be asymptotically rank-one. Require proper invariant K, K intersect closure(H(F)) = {0}, and positive antinorm; bound gap tends to selected delta > 0. No unrestricted computability conclusion.

proposition: Operator Schmidt rank equals the ordinary matrix rank of realignment for the specified finite-dimensional bipartite tensor decomposition.
notes: The preprint title is Restrictions on the Schmidt rank of bipartite unitary operators beyond dimension two. Do not extend this identity to arbitrary multipartite tensor rank.
